4a(1).fact: Group participation builds lasting ethical values, adult mentorship, and mutual social responsibility that guide positive choices even when youths are unsupervised.
4a(1).misconception: Youth clubs and sports teams reduce crime solely by filling up free time on the calendar.
4a(1).pamphlet_summary: Active involvement in civic, religious, and athletic groups establishes strong personal character and accountability while providing supervised alternatives to idle time on the street. These shared community networks reinforce positive peer pressure and encourage neighbors to look out for one another (p. 35).
4a(1).socratic_question: Why do neighborhood sports leagues and youth groups often result in lower local vandalism rates even after the season ends?

4a(2).fact: Concealing barriers and high shrubbery actually aid burglars by blocking sightlines from the street and providing hidden areas to force entry undetected.
4a(2).misconception: Tall privacy fences and overgrown perimeter hedges provide the best defense against residential burglary.
4a(2).pamphlet_summary: Proper environmental design uses natural surveillance, defined property boundaries, and controlled access points to eliminate hiding spots and deter potential offenders. Keeping shrubbery trimmed below window level and maintaining adequate exterior lighting allow neighbors and passersby to observe unusual activity easily (p. 38).
4a(2).socratic_question: If a homeowner installs an eight-foot solid wooden privacy fence around the front yard, how might that actually make things easier for a burglar?
